2_Introduction: The PCE of the device was increased to 11.5943% with an FF of 53.2607%, VOC of 1.0652 V and JSC of 20.437 mA/cm². A perovskite precursor solution was first prepared using Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 at 1.73 mol/L. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating at 1100 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the spin-coating, 170 µL CB solution was dripped at 5 s before the end of the spin-coating process. The films were then annealed at 100 °C for 20 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The mixed-cation perovskite Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 and reduced halide vacancy formation energy due to partial Br⁻ substitution—undergoes kinetically controlled crystallization wherein the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, dual-speed spin-coating (1100 rpm for nucleation followed by 5000 rpm for shear-driven alignment), and precisely timed antisolvent quenching at 5 s before spin cessation collectively suppress premature aggregation, promote uniform nucleation density, and extend the metastable sol–gel transition window, thereby minimizing pinholes, suppressing PbI₂ residual phase formation, and mitigating interfacial strain that would otherwise accelerate ion migration and non-radiative recombination at grain boundaries; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this baseline formulation, the absence of extrinsic modifiers renders the intrinsic defect physics of the perovskite layer dominant—where the high FA⁺ content stabilizes the black α-phase while Cs⁺ and MA⁺ jointly suppress phase segregation under thermal stress, and the slight Br⁻ incorporation tunes the bandgap toward optimal charge extraction while enhancing lattice rigidity and reducing halide mobility—yet the modest FF of 53.2607% and VOC of 1.0652 V relative to state-of-the-art devices indicate persistent interfacial recombination and incomplete film coverage, consistent with the implied morphological limitations inferred from the necessity of antisolvent quenching and moderate annealing (100 °C, 20 min), which—while sufficient to volatilize residual DMSO and complete crystallization—fails to fully heal sub-surface iodide vacancies or eliminate nanoscale roughness that disrupts charge transport continuity, as further corroborated by the relatively low PCE of 11.5943% and JSC of 20.437 mA/cm².
